Rolex · ref. 126600

Sea-Dweller

Dive · 40–43mm · 610m–1,220m · automatic

The Rolex Sea-Dweller is a line of professional dive watches designed for saturation diving, defined by its robust construction and a helium escape valve for deep-sea exploration. Signature design cues include a date function, a black dial, and a unidirectional rotating bezel.

The story

The Sea-Dweller was developed in the late 1960s to address the needs of professional saturation divers, whose watches were being damaged by helium buildup during decompression. The key innovation was the helium escape valve, first introduced on the reference 1665 in 1967. Over the years, the Sea-Dweller has seen significant upgrades, including increased water resistance, the introduction of a sapphire crystal with the reference 16660, and more advanced in-house movements. The case size remained at 40mm for decades before being increased to 43mm in 2017 with the reference 126600, which also controversially added a Cyclops lens over the date for the first time in the model's history.

References by era

16651967–c. 1983
The original Sea-Dweller, featuring a helium escape valve and an acrylic crystal. Early models are known as "Double Red Sea-Dwellers" for the two lines of red text on the dial.
166601978–1989
Known as the "Triple Six," this transitional reference introduced a sapphire crystal, a larger helium escape valve, and an increased depth rating to 1,220 meters (4,000 feet).
166001989–2009
A long-running reference that solidified the modern Sea-Dweller's features with an upgraded movement and bracelet.
1166002014–2017
Marked the return of the Sea-Dweller after a brief hiatus, featuring a Cerachrom ceramic bezel and a 40mm case.
1266002017–present
The 50th-anniversary model, which increased the case size to 43mm and added a Cyclops lens over the date. It features red "Sea-Dweller" text, echoing the original models.
